text:
marta: Customer on prod reporting streaming sessions drop on reconnects. They see a 401 on second connection after CLF edge, then client retries and gets partial output duplicated. Context: webapp sets auth cookie + uses Cloudflare Spectrum + ALB in front of RVA. Repro intermittently, higher with longer idle. Ticket: #SUP-9123 :eyes:
alex: Can you paste the raw request/response headers for the failed reconnect? Especially `Authorization` vs cookie behavior. Also which model / route?
marta: Route is /v1/stream/chat -> model: redwood-medium-8k. Attached headers from their proxy logs (redacted):
```
GET /v1/stream/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Cookie: session=****; path=/; HttpOnly
Authorization: Bearer r_live_xxx
Connection: keep-alive
User-Agent: client/1.2.3
```
Response (on reconnect attempt #2):
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: session=; Max-Age=0; Path=/
Connection: close
```
ben: Hm. Two hypotheses: 1) Cloudflare is reusing an edge connection and passing a cached/expired cookie on reconnect, triggering auth revoke. 2) ALB idle timeout + client TCP half-close leads the app to treat it as new session and triggering logout. Both could cause duplicate partial chunks if client reconnects without resume token.
ryan: Also check NLB vs ALB vs Envoy behavior for half-close and FIN handling. NLB often does TCP-level half-close that can hide idle resets from the app. ALB has 60s idle timeout default. Cloudflare has its own keepalive heuristics. :thinking:
marta: Customer repro steps simplified: 1) Start stream, let it produce ~120 tokens. 2) Idle for ~75s. 3) Client reconnects with same `Authorization` header and no explicit resume-id. Sometimes second connection returns 401 immediately. When 401 happens, client retries fast -> we see two short streams (partial) and they get charged twice.
alex: Can you share short server logs around the 401? Specifically correlation id or request ids (X-Request-Id / X-Trace).
marta: Pasted sample lines from their proxied logs:
```
[2025-08-10T12:01:17Z] req=ab12 model=redwood-medium-8k conn=192.0.2.14:34567 -> 10.1.2.3:443 FIN_WAIT
[2025-08-10T12:02:32Z] req=ab13 auth=expired reason=token_revoked status=401 set-cookie:del
[2025-08-10T12:02:33Z] req=ab14 stream_start token_count=12
[2025-08-10T12:02:33Z] req=ab15 stream_start token_count=9
```
ben: Looks like token_revoked event between connections. Could be a session rotation on the auth server triggered by proxied healthcheck? Any WAF or session refresh flows?
marta: Customer says no explicit logout. They use a short-lived session cookie refreshed by their backend every minute. If refresh hits during idle, Cloudflare may route to a different origin that responds with no valid cookie, causing 401.
ryan: For immediate mitigation: 1) recommend client send an explicit `X-Resume-Token` header created on initial stream so server can detect duplicate/resumed sessions and avoid double-billing. 2) Increase ALB idle timeout to >120s or enable ALB keepalive. 3) On our side, treat immediate reconnect within Xs for same user & stream as resume, not new billable start.
support-bot: Created internal ticket INF-5412 to track server-side de-dupe for rapid reconnects and billing variance. Linked customer SUP-9123.
infra-oncall: Also add note to check Cloudflare pool affinity/healthchecks. If healthcheck hits their auth backend and rotates session, that could explain token_revoked. We saw similar in eng-infra last quarter.
marta: Quick repro curl (client-side):
```
# start stream
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/chat
# wait 80s, then reconnect
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/chat
```
If second returns 401, steps above reproduce.
alex: Thanks. Next steps: ask customer to 1) try with ALB idle timeout bumped to 180s, 2) try setting cf-connecting-ip/preserve client session (Cloudflare affinity) or disable healthcheck overlap, 3) attach X-Request-Id for us to correlate. We'll follow-up and update INF-5412. :thumbsup:
marta: I'll send the mitigations now. Also adding note: product should consider server-side `retry-after` or idempotency token for streams to avoid duplicate billing when reconnect loops happen.
ben: Agreed. Will add to INF-5412 backlog for eval.
ryan: I'll add a runbook snippet for oncall: how to triage streaming 401 after idle and how to check ALB/CF/NLB logs.
support-bot: Noted. Ticket INF-5412 updated with runbook link.
